title: Principal Research Scientist - Machine Learning
description: <p>IMC is one of the world’s leading trading firms, combining quantitative research, technology and trading expertise to solve complex problems at scale.</p> <p>As Machine Learning becomes increasingly important within our Systematic Equities business, we are investing in frontier research that can shape the next generation of models, infrastructure and research capabilities. With access to world-class datasets, significant compute resources and a highly collaborative environment, IMC offers a unique opportunity to see cutting-edge research translated into real-world impact.</p> <p>We are seeking a Principal Research Scientist to help define and accelerate our long-term machine learning research agenda. Prior finance experience is not required.</p> <h2>The Role</h2> <p>This role is designed for an established academic researcher or research scientist who wants to remain connected to the frontier of machine learning while applying their expertise in a highly impactful environment.</p> <p>You will work alongside quantitative researchers, engineers and research leadership to identify emerging research directions, evaluate new developments in machine learning, and help translate promising academic advances into practical applications.</p> <p>Rather than owning individual trading strategies, you will act as a scientific leader, mentor and advisor across the research organisation. You will also represent IMC externally through participation in leading conferences and engagement with the broader machine learning community.</p> <h2>Responsibilities</h2> <ul> <li>Shape the long-term machine learning research agenda within Systematic Equities.</li> <li>Identify and translate advances from frontier ML research into practical opportunities.</li> <li>Conduct original research and develop proof-of-concept solutions where appropriate.</li> <li>Advise and mentor quantitative researchers on methodology, experimentation and research direction.</li> <li>Help guide future investments in research tooling, infrastructure and compute capabilities.</li> <li>Represent IMC within the global machine learning community through conferences such as NeurIPS, ICML and ICLR.</li> <li>Contribute to publication efforts where appropriate and consistent with intellectual property considerations.</li> </ul> <h2>Skills & Experience</h2> <ul> <li>PhD in Machine Learning, Computer Science, Statistics, Mathematics, Physics or a related quantitative discipline.</li> <li>Outstanding academic credentials and a strong publication record in leading research venues.</li> emerging research trends.</li> <li>Experience influencing research direction, mentoring researchers, or leading research initiatives.</li> <li>Strong programming skills and experience with modern machine learning frameworks.</li> <li>Excellent communication skills and the ability to collaborate across disciplines.</li> </ul> <h2>What We Offer</h2> <ul> <li>The opportunity to influence the title: Sales & Client Engagement Director (EMEA + DACH)
description: <h2>About us</h2> <p><a href="https://constructorlabs.org/">Constructor Labs</a> is the research arm of Constructor Knowledge, based at Campus Ring 1 in Bremen, Germany. Our work is organized around three units: Knowledge Labs, Cyber Labs and Science Labs. We apply computing, software and robotics research to make scientists, teachers and students more effective, working with institutional partners that include CERN, NUS, Carnegie Mellon and Fraunhofer.</p> <p>Our <a href="https://constructorlabs.org/solutions/edtech/">EdTech practice</a> produces research that runs in production. AI-supported remote proctoring is in use at the Irish Aviation Authority, Princess Nourah University and Saudi Electronic University, and our course delivery platform is used by CERN, EPFL, MariaDB and Acronis. For industry clients, we build tailored BSc, MSc and PhD pipelines, L&D operating models, AI upskilling programmes and customer training systems.</p> <p><strong>Constructor Labs Solutions (CLS)</strong> is our client-facing systems integrator for the education and research sector, launching in September 2026. It brings audit and consultancy, content, platform, talent and R&D services together under a single contract, an offer few providers make to education buyers today. Delivery is orchestrated across several Constructor organizations: CUB, Nexford, Nexademy, EBAC, Constructor Labs and Constructor Tech. Our aim is to become the go-to systems integrator for education in EMEA by 2029.</p> <h2>The role</h2> <p>You will open EMEA markets for Constructor Labs Solutions as a quota-carrying individual contributor. The role rests on an established network among universities, online education providers, EdTech vendors and corporate L&D and research buyers, and on your ability to convert that network into signed engagements.</p> <p>You will work with the marketing and delivery teams to build pipeline, establish the CLS brand and develop a case-study library. Supporting you are a credible research institution, named production references, an existing Constructor and Constructor Tech client base, and delivery capability across five service lines that can be combined into a single proposal.</p> <p>The sales motion is consultative. Engagements typically open with a low-risk paid diagnostic (Technology Landscape Assessment, Curriculum Gap Analysis or Learning Strategy Advisory), which you then convert into a multi-line implementation or managed-service mandate. Initial engagements start at around €150–250K in lifetime value and grow from there. Sales cycles in public higher education run six to twelve months, so you will manage a long-cycle institutional funnel alongside faster corporate L&D deals.</p> <h2>Reporting and scope</h2> <ul> <li><strong>Reports to:</strong> Director of Sales & Marketing, Constructor Labs Solutions (shared with the Constructor Labs GM during Phase 1).</li> <li><strong>Level:</strong> Director, individual contributor. You will join an established sales team.</li> <li><strong>Territory:</strong> EMEA, with initial focus on DACH (Germany, Austria, Switzerland) and the UK and Ireland. Named accounts agreed quarterly.</li> <li><strong>Segments:</strong> traditional and online universities, EdTech providers and platform vendors, corporate L&D and corporate academies, research-intensive organizations, and publicly funded research programmes.</li> <li><strong>Portfolio:</strong> all five CLS service lines, namely Audit & Consultancy, Content, Platform, Talent and R&D Services.</li> </ul> <p>Day-to-day, you will work with the Audit & Consultancy Practice Head on scoping, with Nexademy on content propositions, with Constructor Tech on platform architecture, and with the Labs' principal investigators, who join client conversations to provide subject-matter credibility. Knowing which expert belongs in which conversation is central to the role.</p> <h2>What you will do</h2> <ul> <li><strong>Pipeline generation.</strong> Around 70% of your time is spent on outbound activity: your own network, conference presence, sector associations, procurement frameworks and targeted account campaigns, supported by marketing.</li> <li><strong>Reference accounts.</strong> Sign the first reference clients in EMEA and develop each one into a published case study, an active sponsor and a source of introductions.</li> <li><strong>Discovery and scoping.</strong> Map the client's learning or research operating model and quantify the problem in their own measures: cost per course, time to accreditation, completion rates, time-to-hire, research throughput. Shape a diagnostic that leads to a defined follow-on engagement.</li> <li><strong>Conversion to implementation.</strong> Own the transition from paid diagnostic to multi-line mandate, with a target of converting half of all audit engagements.</li> <li><strong>Proposals and bids.</strong> Assemble proposals across the five service lines with the practice heads, price them against the finance model and qualify them against margin floors. Lead RFP and framework responses, including public-sector tenders in Germany and the UK.</li> <li><strong>Stakeholder coverage.</strong> Engage rectors, deans, CIOs, heads of digital learning, procurement, works councils, CLOs, HR directors and research directors. Maintain at least three engaged contacts on every opportunity above €200K.</li> <li><strong>Partner channel.</strong> Recruit and manage regional partners, resellers, agencies and academic networks that extend reach beyond your direct coverage.</li> <li><strong>Quota and forecasting.</strong> You carry an annual new-business quota, with quarterly KPIs covering pipeline coverage, audit conversion, average engagement value and blended margin. Maintain weekly pipeline hygiene in the CRM, submit a forecast you can defend, and flag slippage as soon as you see it.</li> <li><strong>Market feedback.</strong> Report what EMEA buyers procure and what they decline, and how our pricing compares with Instructure, D2L, Cornerstone and the generalist integrators, so that the service catalogue can be adjusted.</li> <li><strong>External representation.</strong> Speak at sector events and contribute to thought leadership alongside our principal investigators, building recognition for CLS among education buyers in your region.</li> </ul> <h2>Targets and KPIs</h2> <p>The role carries a quota set on net-new signed bookings (total contract value) in your territory, with a six-month ramp and a quarterly review:</p> <ul> <li>Net-new signed bookings (TCV)</li> <li>Reference clients signed</li> <li>Average engagement value</li> <li>Audit-to-implementation conversion</li> <li>Blended gross margin on signed work</li> <li>New qualified opportunities created</li> <li>Forecast accuracy</li> </ul> <h2>What you bring</h2> <ul> <li><strong>Network in the sector.</strong> Eight or more years selling into education, research or corporate learning in EMEA, preferably DACH and/or the UK, with decision-maker relationships you can open within the first 90 days. You should be prepared to discuss your top 15 target accounts and the route into each.</li> <li><strong>A closing record in complex services.</strong> Consistent achievement against a quota of €1M or more in professional services, consulting, systems integration or enterprise EdTech, covering six-figure deals, multi-stakeholder buying groups and six- to twelve-month cycles.</li> <li><strong>Consultative selling.</strong> Experience selling scoped engagements whose deliverables were defined jointly with the client, and fluency in a recognized methodology such as MEDDIC, Challenger or Command of the Message.</li> <li><strong>Domain credibility.</strong> The ability to hold a substantive conversation with a pro-vice-chancellor about digitalization, a CLO about competency frameworks or a research director about co-funded projects, together with a working understanding of how universities and research organizations buy: budget cycles, committee approval, procurement frameworks and public tender rules.</li> <li><strong>Comfort in an early-stage unit.</strong> Experience building a territory or a new offering from a standing start, and the ability to sell a service catalogue that is still being completed.</li> <li><strong>Languages.</strong> Business-fluent <strong>German</strong> and <strong>English</strong>. Both are required, since public education buyers in DACH contract in German.</li> <li><strong>Commercial discipline.</strong> Rigorous CRM and forecasting practice, and a readiness to qualify out early rather than carry unlikely deals.</li> <li><strong>Professional integrity.</strong> You will represent a research institution to universities and public bodies, so commitments made during the sales process must be ones delivery can meet.</li> </ul> <h2>Nice to have</h2> <ul> <li>Experience selling into publicly funded research programmes, or EU and national grant-co-funded projects (Horizon Europe, Innovate UK, BMBF).</li> <li>Working knowledge of the LMS/SIS landscape and its incumbents — Instructure, D2L, Cornerstone, Moodle, SAP SuccessFactors.</li> <li>Experience with UK public procurement frameworks (Crown Commercial Service, JISC) or German public tendering (VgV, e-Vergabe).</li> <li>Background in the education practice of a systems integrator, Big Four firm or consultancy.</li> <li>Prior success selling talent, recruitment or academic content services.</li> <li>French, Italian or Dutch as a third language.</li> <li>An existing speaking profile in the education or L&D community.</li> </ul> <h2>Location and travel</h2> <p>Candidates must be based in Europe and hold an existing, unrestricted right to work in their country of residence. <strong>Relocation is not offered for this position:</strong> the network the role depends on should already be in the market.</p> <p>Preferred bases are Germany, Switzerland, Bulgaria or the UK. The role is remote or hybrid, with regular time in Bremen and at the London commercial hub. Expect travel of up to 40% within EMEA for client meetings, tenders and sector events, plus occasional travel to other Constructor locations.</p> <h2>What we offer</h2> <ul> <li><strong>Base salary and commission</strong>, weighted approximately 60/40 at on-target earnings, with accelerators above 100% of quota. The band is competitive for a Director-level individual contributor in DACH or the UK and depends on location and experience.</li> <li><strong>A guaranteed ramp</strong> across the first two quarters while the pipeline is built.</li> <li><strong>Commission on margin as well as revenue</strong>, so that well-scoped work is rewarded ahead of discounted work.</li> <li><strong>Access to our researchers</strong>, including principal investi

At MFG, we have a dedicated team of digital B2B and direct response (DR) experts across strategy, activation, planning, analytics, data strategy and client services. Our mission is to drive SMBs to spend their marketing budget within the Google Ads Portfolio (e.g. Google Ads, YouTube Ads etc).</p> <p><strong>About the Client Services team</strong></p> <p>The Client Services team is responsible for creating the conditions by which our clients love our work. title: Associate Director, Client Leadership
description: <div class="content-intro"><p><strong>About WPP Media</strong></p> <p>WPP is the trusted growth partner for the world’s leading brands. With exceptional talent, trusted data and intelligence, and world-class partnerships – all united by our pioneering agentic marketing platform, WPP Open – we help clients navigate change, capture opportunity, and deliver transformational growth. </p> <p>WPP Media is WPP's AI-driven media operating unit, bringing together media, data, and partnerships to deliver creative personalisation at scale. Connected through WPP Open and powered by Open Intelligence, clients see exactly where, how, and why their media investment is working.</p> <p>For more information, visit <a href="wppmedia.com">wppmedia.com</a>.</p></div><p><strong>3809 - Associate Director, Client Leadership - UK</strong></p> <p><strong>Role Summary and Impact</strong></p> <p>We are looking for an enthusiastic, creative, curious Associate Director to join our UK Connections Planning team working on the Unilever Account.</p> <p>Unilever is one of the world’s and UK’s leading FMCG companies, with an incredible portfolio of household names. Unilever’s product portfolio comprises four business groups; Beauty & Wellbeing, Personal Care products, Homecare products and Food. They have a long-standing heritage of putting their customers at the heart of everything they do – and leading with the principles of driving positive change through their brands.</p> <p>The Connections Planning team plays a crucial role in designing the audiences, connections, content and measurement that deliver the most innovative and effective solutions to clients. To do this requires a team of people with a high degree of knowledge of the UK media market and a deep understanding of the role of technology in driving opportunities to target audiences, its impact on the connections and content that will engage people, and how media can be measured and optimised.</p> <p>We foster a highly collaborative environment with brilliant, forward-thinking clients who are not only engaged but genuinely enthusiastic about pushing boundaries. This partnership allows us to deliver truly exciting, market-leading work that sets industry benchmarks and drives significant impact.</p> <p>Expect a role that is highly strategic, requiring deep analytical thinking, a keen commercial eye, and a flair for innovative solutions. We are consistently exploring new technologies, channels, and audience engagement models, ensuring your work remains at the cutting edge. Innovation is not just encouraged, it's expected.</p> <p>Crucially, you'll have seamless access to a rich tapestry of agency expertise. You'll collaborate daily with our specialist teams in data science, advanced measurement & analytics, brand strategy, and consumer insights. This integrated approach empowers you to craft media plans that are not only creative and impactful but also deeply informed, measurable, and strategically sound.</p> <p><strong><u>About the role</u></strong></p> <p>You will be expected to demonstrate experience and knowledge in -</p> <ul> <li>Knowing the tools and means to build and target audiences in addressable and non-addressable media to validate the media approach ensuring that the defined audience can be reached at the scale required</li> <li>Designing an approach that outlines how and where we will connect with defined audiences – especially hard to reach / low media engagement audiences – in media for brand and performance campaigns.</li> <li>Connecting the dots between the data we, the client, media owners and other internal teams hold to plan most effectively.</li> <li>Designing the connections ecosystem & plan, working closely and collaboratively with channel specialists and wider agency teams from a paid, owned and earned perspective</li> <li>Day to day management of campaigns and annual planning as a key liaison between clients and channel specialists</li> <li>Designing measurement & testing framework to inform as well as measure and optimise the campaigns when live</li> <li>Management of others to develop their skills</li> </ul> <p><strong>Skills and Experience</strong></p> <p>At WPP Media, we believe in the power of our culture and our people. It’s what elevates us to deliver exceptional experiences for both our clients and each other. In this role it will be critical to embrace WPP & WPP Media’s shared core values:</p> <ul> <li>Be <strong>Extraordinary</strong> by <em>Leading Collectively</em> to <em>Inspire transformational Creativity.</em></li> <li>Create an <strong>Open</strong> environment by<em> Balancing People and Client Experiences</em> by <em>Cultivating Trust</em>.</li> <li>Lead <strong>Optimistically</strong> by <em>Championing Growth</em> <em>and Development</em> to <em>Mobilize the Enterprise</em>.</li> <li>You show a breadth of understanding of all media channels and can confidently discuss the role they play within a comms strategy</li> <li>Have an interest in both brand and performance campaigns with some knowledge of ecommerce</li> <li>You are a tool ‘wizard’...well not quite but excellent knowledge of audience research and planning tools (e.g. TGI & Touchpoints) is a must and awareness of / familiarity with alternative sources (such as media owner tools & data) is a plus</li> <li>Ability to draw clear insights and implications for media (i.e. connecting the outputs of different insight systems successfully)</li> <li>Demonstrate a passion for media and understanding of what makes a great media campaign, tangibly showcasing excellence in planning craft.</li> <li>Take responsibility for the upfront work that needs to happen in order to deliver a great, clear and concise universal brief to the specialist teams that hits the clients' brief on the head</li> <li>You care about proving your campaigns work! How? By being able to create a holistic measurement framework relevant for your brand and applicable to every campaign that is digestible (setting KPI’s methods I.e., which tool/system, necessary tracking) and plan for adaptation/optimisation</li> <li>You are confident in presenting with passion and conviction, managing senior client relationships, running all agency team sessions and collaboratively leading client projects and tackling challenging conversations.</li> <li>You are excited to work as part of a team; immediate, wider department and specialists as required. Leading by example though presence and contribution. Taking the responsibility for working in a collaborative, inclusive way</li> <li>You demonstrate excellent attention to detail and accuracy in output and meeting deadlines. As well as strong organization to meet client expectations, manage workflow for self and junior team members.</li> <li>Demonstrate a proactive desire to continually improve own knowledge and wider skill set</li> <li>You are open minded, flexible and have a challenger mindset.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Life at WPP Media & Benefits</strong></p> <p>Our passion for shaping the next era of media includes investing in our employees to help them do their best work, and we’re just as committed to employee growth as we are to responsible media investment. WPP Media employees can tap into the global WPP Media & WPP networks to pursue their passions, grow their networks, and learn at the cutting edge of marketing and advertising. We have a variety of employee resource groups and host frequent in-office events showcasing team wins, sharing thought leadership, and celebrating holidays and milestone events. Our benefits include competitive medical, group retirement plans, vision, and dental insurance, significant paid time off, preferential partner discounts, and employee mental health awareness days.  </p> <p>WPP Media is an equal opportunity employer and considers applicants for all positions without discrimination or regard to particular characteristics. We are committed to fostering a culture of respect in which everyone feels they belong and has the same opportunities to progress in their careers.<br><br>We believe the best work happens when we're together, fostering creativity, collaboration, and connection. That's why we’ve adopted a hybrid approach, with teams in the office around four days a week. If you require accommodations or flexibility, please discuss this with the hiring team during the interview process.</p> <p><em>Please note this is a UK based role and requires individuals to have the right to work in this location</em></p> <p>Please read our Privacy Notice (<a href="https://www.wppmedia.com/pages/privacy-policy">https://www.wppmedia.com/pages/privacy-policy)</a> for more information on how we process the information you provide.</p> <p>While we appreciate all applications received, only those candidates selected for an interview will be contacted. </p> <p>#LI-Promoted</p><div class="content-conclusion"><p></p> <p><span class="TextRun SCXW227196529 BCX8" lang="EN-CA" data-contrast="auto"><span class="NormalTextRun SCXW227196529 BCX8">Please read our <a href="https://www.wppmedia.com/pages/privacy-policy#:~:text=WPP%20Media%20Privacy%20Notice%20for%20Recruitment">Privacy Notice</a></span></span><span class="TextRun SCXW227196529 BCX8" lang="EN-CA" data-contrast="auto"> <span class="NormalTextRun SCXW227196529 BCX8">for more information on how we process the information you provide.</span></span><span class="EOP SCXW227196529 BCX8" data-ccp-props="{"201341983":0,"335559739":0,"335559740":276}"> </span></p></div> Find more English Speaking Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

title: Partnerships Manager
description: About Dust Work is being rewritten, and the people holding the pen are the ones who actually run it. With enterprise-grade governance, flexible model choice, and a collaborative interface for humans and agents to work together, Dust empowers AI Operators at the world’s fastest-moving companies to rewire how work gets done. With 70%+ weekly active users, people stick with Dust as much as they do with Slack and Notion. We don't get piloted and shelved. We land once, and spread. We're at an exciting stage of our journey, and growing fast. We're serving great customers like Datadog, 1Password, Cursor, Clay, Vanta and Persona, and aim to x5 our growth by the end of 2026. Dust is backed by Sequoia with a determined team of optimists (coming from Stripe, OpenAI, and Stanford) who like to focus on users, ship fast, and don't take themselves too seriously while doing so. The Generalist named us among the Future 50 . This Role Dust is seeking a UK Partnerships Manager to grow our partner ecosystem in the UK. This is a business development role at its core: your job is to identify, engage, and activate the partners who will become a meaningful source of pipeline and revenue for Dust in the UK market. This is a 0-to-1 role. There is no existing UK partner program, no playbook, no team. You'll be the first person on the ground, responsible for building relationships, closing early partnership agreements, and proving that partners can generate real pipeline for Dust. You'll work cross-functionally with Sales, Field Marketing, Growth, Community, the France Partnerships team, and the Executive Team to make this happen. All types of partnerships are in scope: resellers, system integrators, consultancies, agencies, tech alliances, affiliates, community partners, and anything else that drives results. We care about what works, not what fits a predefined category. The Solution Partner Ecosystem is the second biggest growth lever at Dust, yet UK's agency and professional services market is still almost entirely untapped. As Partner Manager UK at Dust, you will build partnerships with leading agencies to boost partner-led revenue. Your job is to find the right partners in the UK, recruit them, and get them to their first win fast, and then transform into a repeatable motion. Working directly with our global partnerships team, you'll own the outreach motion, the onboarding, and the early relationship with every new partner you bring in, primarily AI transformation agencies and consultants. This is a hands-on role for someone who can build a relationship quickly, has entrepreneurial, and can craft joint solutions that makes partners want to invest in Dust. You will be part of a growing global partnerships team of 6 people, with dedicated support from partner operations, solutions engineer and partner marketing. Key Responsibilities Partner Ecosystem Development Build Dust's UK partner ecosystem. Identify, qualify, and recruit the partners best positioned to Dust’s ICP buyers in the UK, Drive partners to pipeline. This isn't about signing partner logos. Your success is measured by partners generating qualified opportunities, co-selling with Dust AEs, and closing deals. Own the full journey from first conversation to first partner-sourced deal Create activation playbooks that take partners from signed agreement to actively selling. Build the training, enablement, and co-selling infrastructure needed to make partners effective Own UK partnership pipeline and revenue targets , with latitude to experiment with creative deal structures, incentive models, and go-to-market approaches Cross-Functional Collaboration Work hand-in-hand with UK Sales (AEs and BDRs) to ensure partners are pipeline accelerators. Build deal routing, co-selling motions, and account mapping that the sales team actually uses Collaborate with Field Marketing (Events, Content, Community) to build joint events, co-branded content, and community activations that serve both partner development and demand generation Stay tightly connected with the Global Partnerships team to share learnings, adapt proven playbooks, and maintain consistency where it matters Partner with Growth Marketing to turn partner activity into scalable demand: co-hosted webinars, joint case studies, partner-led content, and event-driven pipeline Coordinate with Product and Engineering on integration priorities, partner feedback, and joint solution development where relevant Requirements Every candidate and employee's success is measured against the same 3 dimensions. Aptitude, Attitude and Agency. Aptitude High AI literacy, you're already using AI daily in your work and can articulate how you'd apply it to partnerships at Dust Proven go-to-market strategy experience: customer-obsessed, first-principles thinking, not just copy-pasting past playbooks Experience building partnerships at a startup or scale-up (not large enterprise reseller models) Specific experience with agency partners, system integrators, or similar zero-to-one motions Grit and sales acumen, you can convince partners, hold them accountable, and go through windows when doors are closed Attitude Team player who solves for Dust and its customers, not just partnerships metrics Low ego, high impact, you leverage others' work and make the broader team better Decisive — you make tough calls on prioritisation and aren't afraid to cut partnerships that aren't working Direct and transparent, you surface problems early and give honest feedback User-first orientation, you frame decisions around customer outcomes without being prompted Agency You unblock yourself with AI and people, scaling your impact through tools and cross-functional leverage You own outcomes end-to-end, identifying gaps, building solutions, and driving to resolution without being told You challenge the goal when it's wrong, high agency in execution AND thinking You've expanded your scope by solving problems no one assigned you You launch things without waiting for permission and find ways to deliver with limited resources Location We're prioritizing building our team with an in-person culture at our offices in Paris, London, San Francisco, and New York because we value the magic that happens when talented people work closely together. We have an office-first culture. Some of the best things about building at Dust are the energy, the fast decisions, and the unexpected conversations that unlock a hard problem, which happen because we are in the same room. Being together is not a formality, it is how we do our best work, and it is something we actively protect. That said, we hire people with strong judgement and we extend that trust to how they manage their time. When working from home makes more sense for what you need to get done that day, we trust you to make that call. Why Dust The models are powerful enough. What's missing is the product layer where AI meets how companies actually work. That's what we're building: the infrastructure that lets any team turn scattered knowledge and tools into coordinated execution with agents they build, own, and run themselves. We use Dust ourselves every day. We get to shape how humans and agents collaborate while solving our own problems with the product we ship. That loop is rare, and it's why we move fast. If you're excited about defining a new category and want to join a determined team of optimists who focus on users, ship fast, and don't take themselves too seriously, we'd love to talk. Even if you don't check every box in our requirements, we encourage you to apply. We value diverse perspectives and backgrounds, and we're more interested in your potential and passion than a perfect match to our checklist. Learn how we think and work. Our product constitution, a story about our mission Your Next Co-Worker Isn’t Human , Stanislas Polu , VivaTech 2026. A conversation about AI agents taking on larger parts of work and how teams collaborate with them. Dust: Gabriel Hubert on Enterprise AI , Gabriel Hubert , Nasdaq, published May 7, 2026. On Dust’s approach to enterprise AI and building the company in Europe. title: Senior Treasury Operations Analyst
description: Trust unlocks our greatest potential. For decades, the clearing of payments remained unchanged and unchallenged. We asked, what if there was a better way? What if we could make banking infrastructure faster, safer, more reliable, and easier to access for all? Here is where you can think radically and responsibly to find the best solution. What happens when you know you’re inherently trusted? Trust creates safety. Safety encourages you to be brave, to challenge, to fail, to try new things and to execute. At ClearBank everything revolves around trust. We’re not expected to earn it, but we are expected not to break it. We’re trusted to own it. To solve issues in the moment. To know a good risk when we see one, and the judgement to know that ‘can’ doesn’t always mean you ‘should’. What you can expect: ClearBank is a place where you can do things differently and challenge the status quo. We will give you a high level of autonomy and transparency, and we trust you to make the right decisions for the bank. If that excites you, how about joining our Treasury Operations team as a Senior Treasury Operations Analyst? Reporting to the Treasury Operations Lead, you will support Treasury Operations activities across ClearBank Group entities, including cash management, FX settlement, collateral and margin management and related processes. The role is responsible for executing complex operational activity with a high degree of accuracy and control, supporting day‑to‑day Treasury and contributing to the safe, resilient operation of a control‑critical function, while ensuring excellent service to internal and external stakeholders. As a senior member of the team, the role will deputise for the Treasury Operations Lead when required, providing operational leadership on shift, including coaching and direction to team members, while identifying efficiencies and continuous improvements across the function. Please note - This role operates within a shift‑based Treasury Operations environment. Specific shift arrangements are communicated separately and may vary over time. Your role includes: Execute Treasury Operations activities across multiple ClearBank Group entities and multi‑currency Nostro accounts, ensuring accuracy, timeliness and strong control discipline Perform and monitor FX settlement activity with multiple FX providers, resolving issues and exceptions within agreed procedures Support cash and liquidity management processes, working closely with Treasury to manage intraday and end‑of‑day balances Manage collateral and margin activity relating to UK securities, including transfers, settlement and ongoing monitoring of asset sales Ensure all Treasury and cash management instruments, including FX swaps and money market funds, are confirmed and settled without exceptions Deputise for the Treasury Operations Shift Manager when required, leading operational activity on shift and acting as a point of escalation within established BAU and contingency procedures Exercise sound judgement during live operational issues, escalating in a timely manner where there is a high degree of certainty that existing processes or controls may fail Contribute to continuous improvement by identifying opportunities to enhance Treasury Operations processes, controls and workflows Build and maintain effective working relationships with internal teams and, where required, external counterparties to support smooth operational delivery Produce operational reporting and management information as required to support oversight and decision‑making Support the onboarding and operation of new Treasury instruments and products as ClearBank Group’s offering evolves What you’ll bring: To excel in this role, you’ll also need: Experience in Treasury Operations, cash management or payments operations within a regulated financial services environment Strong working knowledge of FX settlement, Nostro account management and liquidity processes Experience managing or supporting collateral and margin activity, including securities settlement Proven ability to operate effectively in a time‑critical or shift‑based environment Sound understanding of operational risk, controls and escalation frameworks Experience producing or contributing to operational reporting and MI Strong communication skills, with the ability to work confidently across teams and with external parties Beneficial skills: Experience supporting multiple legal entities and currencies Exposure to new product or instrument launches within Treasury or Operations Knowledge of UK securities settlement processes and market infrastructure Experience contributing to process improvement or operational change initiatives Regretfully we are not able to sponsor applicants for immigration purposes at the current time. What makes a great ClearBank team member? Does this sound like you? You focus on solutions and positive outcomes, thinking radically and responsibly to find the best result for our customers, your colleagues and the bank; You actively seek feedback from others to drive your growth and development, always assuming positive intent from others and develop strong, trusting relationships you’re your colleagues and customers: you really, genuinely care; You always strive for the highest quality, but you know that done is better than perfect; you welcome a challenge knowing that they learn as you go and iterate; ‘I’ before ’we’, isn’t in your vocabulary If this sounds like you then we encourage you to dust off that CV and apply! What we offer in return: We're flexible – We support a culture of flexibility which allows our employees to achieve a strong work-life balance. Offices – Work in a way that works for you – whether that’s in the London office, at home, or hybrid. Holiday – 27 days of annual leave per year, plus bank holidays. Holiday buy/sell - Buy or sell up to five days of annual leave each year and shape your year around what matters most. Work abroad – You have the flexibility to work outside of the UK for up to 30 days in a rolling 12-month period. Socials – Regular social events open to all. Holiday swap – Option to swap your bank holidays to any other day of your choice. Wellbeing – 24/7 employee assistance programme including mental health support, life assurance and income protection. Bigger than ClearBank – Take a couple of days per year to do something that matters to you. Healthy living – Private healthcare and discounted dental cover, with employee perks and discounts. Family – Enhanced family-friendly leave. Personal development – We offer personal development budgets, opportunities to take part in role-related training and unlimited LinkedIn Learning. And not forgetting the biggest benefit of all. The opportunity to be part of an incredible team that’s building a tech-bank fit for the future. A little bit more about us! ClearBank is Where You Can belong: At ClearBank we think about Diversity, Equity and Inclusion (DE&I) a lot. Not because we think we should. But because we know we should – how else can we build a happy workforce and be successful as a business. We’re committed to making sure our teams reflect society. And we put energy and effort into making this a place where everyone feels at home, where they’re given the trust and encouragement to do their very best work. Here are some of the things we’re most proud of: 42% of our senior management roles are held by women Our enhanced family leave policies Launching our partnership with Code First Girls Increasing awareness of neurodiversity in the workplace through our partnership with the Inclusive Group Our hiring process and what you can expect: Application: a member of our talent acquisition team will review your application against the key requirements for the role and let you know within two weeks whether you’re moving forward to the next stage; Screening: You’ll spend 30-45 minutes speaking to one of our recruiters learning more about the role and ClearBank, and we’ll get it know more about you, your experience and how your skills align with the role (this will be via phone or Teams video call). You can expect to hear back from us within seven days following this meeting (if things are taking longer than expected, we’ll let you know that too); First Interview: You’ll spend one hour with a member of our hiring team focusing on your skills, competencies and your ways of working at the same time we’ll give you time to ask more questions about the role, the team and learn more about the ClearBank culture. This will be via Teams. Second Interview: This will be a competency-based interview with one or more members of our team. Final Stage: You will have a final meeting with the Head of Department. This will be around 45-60 minutes. Offer: Congratulations! Get ready to transform banking forever! Our commitment to you as a candidate: We will always try our best to get back to you within seven days of your interview whether you’ve been successful or not and provide you with feedback. Sometimes things take a little longer, so we may not have a decision to share but we will get it touch to let you know we need a little more time. We’re unable to provide specific individual feedback at the application or screening stage but know that your application was reviewed and considered carefully. We wish you the best of luck with your application and maybe we’ll be celebrating your new role at ClearBank soon! Equal Opportunities ClearBank is committed to ensuring equal opportunities throughout every stage of the recruitment process. ClearBank recognises that diversity is vital to the long-term success of the business in the communities and markets in which it operates. ClearBank is also a firm believer that an inclusive culture fosters greater employee engagement and collaboration. ClearBank strives for diversity and inclusion of all forms, including (but not limited to): gender, age, educational and professional background, disability, gender reassignment, marital or civil partner status, pregnancy or maternity, race, colour, nationality, ethnic or national origin, religion or belief and sexual orientation. As part of the Company’s commitment to equal employment opportunity, we provide reasonable adjustments, to candidates during the recruitment process, including to individuals with disabilities. We want to create a safe space that welcomes everyone so please let us know how we can accommodate you. In case you have any accessibility requirements you can share that with our Talent Acquisition team prior to your interview stage, if applicable. title: Senior Security Engineer
description: Hi 👋 I’m Nitesh, Engineering Manager at hyperexponential. I'm one for the career mentors in the Product Foundations stream. We tackle the fundamental problems every product team at hx runs into, so the vertical streams can focus on building features for customers. Right now that means deployments, observability, security, AI observability tooling and a permission service that other value streams will build on. I’m hiring a Senior Security Engineer to join us as our second security hire. The foundations are already in place. We’ve chosen and implemented our tooling, and our repositories and cloud environments are onboarded. The next step is shaping how security actually works here. This won’t be a traditional, hierarchical security function. Our engineers go straight to the person who owns an issue and ask them to fix it, and you’ll help define what security looks like in that model. There’s no established playbook for this yet, which is what makes it exciting. If that sounds like your kind of challenge, I’d love to hear from you. About hyperexponential (hx) At hyperexponential, we're building the AI-powered platform that enables the world's most critical decisions in a £7 trillion industry, which risks to take, and how to price them. These are the decisions that shape real-world outcomes: whether rockets successfully launch into space, autonomous vehicles make it to market, or communities recover after major storms. Until now, insurance has been making billion-pound decisions using outdated tools. We're changing that. Our platform brings together data, AI, and human expertise to give insurers the fastest path from submission to decision - helping them move faster, act smarter, and take on more risk with confidence. Backed by a16z, Highland Europe, and Battery Ventures, we're scaling globally - already trusted by nearly 50 of the world's largest insurers, with zero churn and billions in premiums flowing through hx. What began as a single product in one market has rapidly evolved into a multi-product, multi-territory platform powering every stage of pricing and underwriting. AI is at the core of what we do - from building the world's first domain-specific AI peer programmer for insurance (think GitHub Copilot with a PhD in actuarial science) to shaping agentic workflows that reinvent how this industry operates. What makes hx different is the people who build it. Here, impact isn't tied to title or tenure; it's defined by the challenges you take on and the discipline you bring. Surrounded by peers who stretch you, you'll do the best, hardest work of your life in a company engineered to endure. If that sounds like you, join us in building what comes next. About the Security function The Security function's mission is to safeguard the integrity, confidentiality, and availability of our customers' data and hx's systems. By fostering a culture of vigilance, risk mitigation, and continuous improvement, we maintain the highest standards of security excellence. Security at hx underpins every product and every customer interaction. As we scale our multi-product platform globally and adopt AI across the business, the team ensures that innovation and growth are matched with rigorous security practices. We design controls, shape culture, and guide decisions that protect our business, our customers, and the wider industry. As a Senior Security Engineer, you’ll be the second engineer in our security team, working directly alongside our Staff Security Engineer. The foundations are in place, with our core tooling chosen, rolled out and onboarded across our repositories and cloud environments. Much of how security works at hx is still to be built, though, so you’ll have real autonomy to shape it, with a direct line to the teams who own the issues you find. You’ll strengthen hx’s security posture by driving continuous improvement across our technical teams: owning security reviews, running and extending our security tooling, and turning findings into fixes, often by writing the code or making the infrastructure change yourself. You’ll champion security initiatives across the organisation, help teams adopt AI securely, and use AI to multiply your own impact. This role combines hands-on technical depth, ownership and influence to make security a practical part of how our teams work every day. Check out our Engineering Candidate Hub for a behind the scenes look at the team you would be joining! What you'll be doing Modify, maintain, and extend our security tooling across engineering and IT environments, including CSPM, SAST, SCA, and secret scanning, ensuring it's reliable, well tuned, and genuinely useful to the teams who depend on it. Use our tooling and your own judgement to proactively identify gaps across cloud security, dependencies, secrets, and code. Work with the owning teams (starting with 2 to 3 where the gaps are greatest) to secure their commitment to prioritise remediation, and see it through. Write code and make infrastructure changes yourself to fix security issues and improve our tooling, rather than just recommending improvements. Own security reviews end to end, partnering with engineering teams on new designs, significant changes, and new tools, and working through follow-up questions and challenges until each review is resolved. Take ownership of and complete a medium-sized security project within your first three months. Partner with our IT team on security best practice, helping implement practical improvements in authentication, authorisation, and security hygiene across our corporate environment. Guide teams across the business on adopting AI securely, from assessing new AI tools and use cases to mitigating risks like data leakage and prompt injection, while using AI yourself to increase your impact. Support our compliance programmes, such as ISO 27001 and SOC 2, by helping teams implement and evidence technical controls. Act as a trusted voice for our technical teams, owning security issues raised with them through to resolution and handling the related correspondence. What you'll need to have done Secured AWS cloud environments hands-on: using Cloud Security tooling to find common weaknesses, and fixing them yourself through infrastructure and code changes. Cloud Security experience is required. Secured containerised workloads and infrastructure-as-code, catching issues before they reach production. Experience working with SAST, SCA, and secret scanning tools, including triaging findings, filtering out false positives, and partnering with engineering teams to get real fixes shipped Supported compliance efforts such as ISO 27001, SOC 2, or GDPR by implementing and evidencing technical controls. Used AI to improve your own security work and helped others adopt it safely, with a practical understanding of AI-specific risks such as data leakage, prompt injection, and agents and integrations with excessive permissions. Spotted and addressed non-technical risks, such as weak processes, risky behaviours, and gaps between teams, that can undermine technical security. Discussed security in depth with engineering teams, explaining complex concepts clearly and concisely and influencing teams through to implementation. Taken ownership of security projects and initiatives and driven them to completion independently. You're unlikely to thrive here if You prefer to advise from the sidelines rather than writing code and making the infrastructure changes yourself. You see security as a gatekeeping function rather than a service to the teams you support, whose adoption and trust determine your success. You'd rather wait for direction than take ownership of issues, follow them through to resolution, and manage the correspondence around them. If reading our Culture Document leaves you feeling neutral rather than energised, hx may not be the place where you'll do your best work. We're building something that asks for commitment and conviction, and we want you to feel excited by the opportunity to grow with us. Compensation At hx, we're committed to salary transparency. You'll always have clarity on pay early in the process - our Talent Partner will share details with you during initial conversations - and we're working towards publishing salary information for all roles globally. Because we're building at the intersection of technology/SaaS and insurance, our roles don't always map neatly onto traditional benchmarks. Our approach is to design compensation that's competitive in the market, fair across teams, and aligned with the impact our people make. Equity: We offer equity across all roles at hx, making it a significant component of total compensation. Your Talent Partner will be able to share more details about this. Benefits £5,000 training and conference budget for individual and group development. 25 days of holiday plus 8 bank holidays (33 days total). Company pension scheme via Penfold. Mental health support and therapy via Spectrum.life . Individual wellbeing allowance via Juno. Private healthcare insurance through AXA. Income protection and Life Insurance. Cycle to Work Scheme. Additional perks Top-spec equipment (laptop, screens, adjustable desks, etc.). Regular remote and in-person hackathons, lunch and learns, socials, and game nights. Team breakfasts and lunches, snacks, drinks fridge, and a fun office at The Ministry. Exceptional opportunities for personal development and growth as we build something remarkable together. Interview process Talent Interview (30 minutes) Hiring Manager Interview (60 minutes) Skills Assessment (120 minutes) Values Interview (60 minutes) Meet the CEO (30 minutes) Our commitment to Diversity hxers are at the centre of everything we build. We know that progress depends on diverse perspectives, and we are committed to creating an environment where everyone can thrive, grow, and make an impact. We recognise there is always more to do, and we take responsibility for shaping a workplace that is not only diverse but genuinely inclusive. Diversity is not just the right thing to do, it is key to solving the complex challenges we choose to take on. By welcoming people from all backgrounds and experiences, we strengthen our ability to question assumptions, push boundaries, and design solutions that endure. If you're energised by complexity and motivated to grow, we encourage you to apply and join our global team. Next steps If this opportunity resonates with you, we encourage you to apply or share it with your connections! Our dedicated talent team reviews all applications, and we promise to provide feedback regardless of the outcome. For more information about applying and to view other opportunities, you can visit our careers page. Please note that background checks will be conducted as part of the hiring process to ensure compliance with our governance policies. We handle all background checks sensitively and in full compliance with relevant regulations. title: Research Engineer (Materials Foundation Models)
description: About CuspAI CuspAI is the frontier AI company on a mission to solve the breakthrough materials needed to power human progress. While nature took billions of years to perfect molecules, we are harnessing AI to unlock trillion-dollar materials breakthroughs in months, not millennia. Our founding team is the most cited in the world, comprised of world-class researchers in AI, chemistry and engineering. We are working on some of the hardest and most important challenges including energy, clean water, the future of compute, and carbon capture, and this is just the start of what our 'search engine' for next-generation materials will unlock. We invite you to be part of a diverse, innovative team at the intersection of AI and materials science, working to create impactful partnerships that drive innovation, scalability, and industry collaboration. This work matters. Your work matters. We’re on the cusp of the on-demand materials era. Join us. The Role To scale our scientific intelligence and data curation capabilities, we are looking for three Research Engineers * to train and evaluate the foundation models behind our materials discovery platform: representation learning over crystal structures and properties, LLM fine-tuning and post-training for scientific tasks, and the evaluation and data work that makes those models useful. You will work in a small team where each person owns a model end to end, from data and experiment design through training at scale to integration. *Note that you would be joining as a ‘Member of Technical Staff’, but the job title above hopefully helps to explain the nature of this role. Your Impact You will be responsible for building and training specialised foundation models on terabytes of scientific data at massive scale , fundamentally enhancing our platform's multi-modal capabilities . The modalities span crystal structures, properties, text and images. The same goes for compensation, benefits, promotions, transfers, reduction in workforce, recall, training, and education.</p> <p> </p></div> Find more English Speaking Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

Depending on your role, you may collaborate with teammates, systems, and leaders across DoorDash and Wolt. Together, we’re unlocking new possibilities as one global team.</p></div><h2>Your job is to make sure every payout and transaction lands with the right person.</h2> <p>We have spent years getting very good at protecting the things a marketplace has always had to protect: checkout fraud, account takeover, courier abuse. But we are no longer only a marketplace. We now issue banking products, lend to merchants, move instant payouts to couriers, and collect cash on the doorstep. Every one of those is a new way for money to leave the platform.</p> <p>This is a new team, and it owns that surface: fraud wherever money moves through the platform. Who receives it, who lends it, who collects it, and who holds it in a financial account. Think instant payout rails, merchant cash advances, and platform-issued banking and earned-wage products serving millions of couriers and merchants. These are live loss surfaces, and the volume grows with every financial product we launch.</p> <p>We are now looking for a <strong>Backend Engineer (Golang)</strong> to build that protection. You will design and ship real-time detection and automated enforcement for our financial products across DoorDash, Wolt, and Deliveroo. The work is high-throughput, low-latency, and unusually consequential: a rule you ship on Monday can stop a serious loss by Friday. It is also close to greenfield, so you will be setting the patterns every future financial product inherits on day one.</p> <p>This role will be based in <strong>London</strong>, <strong>UK</strong> as one of the founding engineering roles in our London hub, working closely with our teams in Helsinki and Berlin.</p> <h3>What you'll do:</h3> <ul> <li>Build and maintain high-throughput, low-latency backend services in Go that score financial events in real time, including payout enrollments, bank account links, credit applications, and account-to-account transfers.</li> <li>Design fraud detection and automated enforcement for our financial products end to end: from signal collection through to the decision that blocks a fraudulent payout.</li> <li>Build on and extend our shared fraud decisioning platform, so signals, rules, and models work across all three of our brands instead of being rebuilt three times.</li> <li>Partner closely with risk analysts, data scientists, and product managers to turn observed fraud patterns into shipped detection, and to know when a rule, a model, or a product change is the right answer.</li> <li>Work across team boundaries with our account security, payments fraud, and financial product teams. We build on their signals rather than rebuild them, so clean interfaces matter.</li> <li>Contribute to architectural discussions and technical decisions as we establish the fraud infrastructure baseline for financial products, with support from senior engineers on the team.</li> <li>Write well-tested, observable code and help the team hold a high quality bar. In fraud, a silent failure is a loss event.</li> </ul> <h2>Our expectations:</h2> <ul> <li>3 to 6 years of professional software engineering experience, including backend services you have shipped and owned in production.</li> <li>1+ years of production experience in Golang, or strong experience in another backend language and real enthusiasm for picking Go up quickly.</li> <li>A working understanding of low-latency, high-throughput distributed systems. Real-time decisioning comes with a latency budget, and you are keen to learn to build inside one.</li> <li>Hands-on experience with SQL and/or NoSQL databases, and some exposure to event-driven architectures (Kafka or similar).</li> <li>Willingness to operate what you build, including a share of on-call, with a pragmatic approach to reliability.</li> <li>Uses AI tooling in day-to-day development and can critically evaluate its output for correctness and quality.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Nice to have</strong></p> <ul> <li>Experience in fraud, risk, payments, lending, or financial crime, especially money movement fraud, bank account linking fraud, payout abuse, or lending fraud.</li> <li>Experience with rules engines, real-time feature stores, or ML model serving in a decisioning path.</li> <li>Background in Kotlin, Java, Python, or Node.js alongside Go.</li> <li>Familiarity with cloud infrastructure (AWS, GCP).</li> <li>Experience working across multiple brands, regions, or regulatory regimes.</li> </ul> <p><strong>What we value</strong></p> <ul> <li>A product-oriented mindset. You think beyond the ticket, understand the "why" behind the work, and take a high level of responsibility for outcomes rather than output.</li> <li>Comfort with ambiguity. This is a new team on a new surface; parts of the charter are still being drawn, and you will help draw them.</li> <li>A track record of owning a project or feature end to end, especially in fast-paced environments.</li> <li>Clear and proactive communication, with a collaborative spirit. title: Staff Software Engineer, Storage Platform
description: Before the detail, here's the challenge you'd help us solve. We build the embodied intelligence that moves real vehicles safely, and the ecosystem a billion machines will run on in the future. Very few people in AI can say this. Every role here, whatever the team, plugs into that. Here’s what this particular role covers. 🛠️ About our AI Platform Teams Our AI Platform teams build the infrastructure that powers Wayve’s embodied AI. We store and serve hundreds of petabytes of driving data, growing towards exabyte scale, to support model training, simulation and data pipelines across regions and clouds. As our first dedicated Staff Software Engineer for Storage Platform, you’ll set the technical direction for how we manage, protect and serve this data. Working closely with Infrastructure, Security, Privacy, Data Engineering and ML teams, you’ll help make training more efficient while reducing one of Wayve’s largest infrastructure costs. 🧠 Your day-to-day Lead a hands-on, multi-quarter storage programme, from defining the problems and architecture to delivering platforms that teams adopt. Build production services, controllers and infrastructure using Python, Go or a similar language, alongside Kubernetes and Terraform. Partner with ML and data teams to understand access patterns, remove storage bottlenecks and reduce the time GPUs spend waiting for data. Work with Security and Privacy to strengthen access controls, auditing and safe deletion of vehicle-collected data. Write design documents and RFCs, align teams around shared standards, and mentor engineers as the platform and team grow. 🧩 What you’ll be working on Data ownership and governance: Give datasets clear owners, purposes and retention classes, with tagging and team-level cost attribution. Safe lifecycle management: Build retention, deletion and re-tiering capabilities for Azure Blob, backed by dry runs, audit trails and recovery paths. Read performance and caching: Improve throughput and latency by tackling small-object reads, throttling, unnecessary data access and cross-region hops. Secure data movement: Design Kubernetes-native NVMe caching and secure replication across regions and clouds. Measurable platform outcomes: Establish standards, dashboards and SLOs for availability, performance, cache effectiveness, storage tiers and cost. 🙌 You should apply if You’ve operated at Staff Engineer scope, leading complex infrastructure programmes across multiple teams from problem definition through adoption. You’ve owned petabyte-scale object storage end to end—including data layout, lifecycle management, performance and cost—with measurable outcomes against a cost target. You’ve built scalable systems for data ownership, tagging, cataloguing, retention or deletion. You bring strong security and access-management experience, including IAM/RBAC, encryption, secure replication and auditing. You’re a hands-on software engineer with strong Python, Go or comparable skills, plus production Kubernetes, Terraform and CI experience. You build durable platforms and services, not just one-off scripts. You can influence technical decisions without formal authority, mentor others and are excited to start in a founding, hands-on role with the opportunity to grow a team. You can work on a hybrid basis from our London office. Experience with AWS or GCP is welcome—you don’t need to have worked exclusively with Azure. 🌱 Not ticking every box? That’s totally okay! If you’re passionate about autonomy and keen to learn, we encourage you to apply even if you don’t meet every requirement. More about Wayve: 🚀 Wayve is building the leading AI platform for autonomous driving. We are pioneering an end to end AI approach that enables vehicles to learn directly from real world experience, developing the ability to adapt, generalise and improve at scale. Instead of relying on hand coded rules or pre mapped environments, our AI Driver learns to drive by understanding the world around it. The result is technology that navigates complex urban environments with intelligence, precision and natural flow, unlocking meaningful advances in both safety and efficiency. We believe autonomy represents a once in a generation transformation in how people and goods move, comparable to the shift from horses to cars, and from human driven vehicles to intelligent machines. Our ambition is to make autonomy universal. Wayve’s mapless and hardware agnostic AI platform integrates with global OEM partners, enabling continuous software evolution and unlocking advanced levels of automation from L2 plus through to L4 as our core AI model scales. In a race increasingly defined by intelligence and real world learning, Wayve is taking a distinct approach, building a generalisable driving intelligence that can power any vehicle, anywhere. By combining embodied AI with scalable deployment, we are creating technology that can be shaped to each OEM brand and driver experience, accelerating the transition to a safer, more intelligent future of mobility. How we work 💻- Locations & Flexible Working: Our main hubs are in London, Sunnyvale, Yokohama, Herzliya, Vancouver and Leonberg. We operate a hybrid working model that combines in-person collaboration in our dedicated office spaces with focused time working remotely. This gives our teams the connection and energy of working together, alongside the flexibility to do their best work in a way that fits their lives. 🔍 The Interview Process: Our process is clear and respectful of your time: Initial call / recruiter screen (30 mins) - A conversation with our Talent Partner about your experience, interest in the role and practical details. Competency Interviews (60 mins) - A programming interview to assess your hands-on software engineering skills. Deep-dive technical interviews - A system design interview and a domain-specific interview with the Hiring Manager, exploring your storage experience, technical leadership and approach to the role. Final interview (30 mins) - Mission & values alignment We’ll always explain the format and work around your availability. What’s in it for you (Location dependant): 💰 Salaries benchmarked against the market annually 📈 Meaningful equity, sharing in the ownership and long term success of Wayve ✈️ Relocation support and visa sponsorship where applicable ✅ Hybrid working, core hours and the chance to work hands on in vehicle workshops and labs 📚 Learning and development budgets with support for training, conferences and growth 🩺 Comprehensive benefits including health insurance, dental, enhanced maternity and paternity leave, retirement or pension where applicable, access to therapists, wellbeing partnerships, team socials and more A quick, honest note before you apply. Wayve is not a mature, fully-structured place with the playbook already written. Much of how we work is still being written, and if you join, you’ll help write it. That suits people who want real ownership more than people who need a settled structure from day one. If that sounds like the kind of problem you want to spend your time on, we’d really like to hear from you. At Wayve we're committed to creating a diverse, fair and respectful culture that is inclusive of everyone based on their unique skills and perspectives, and regardless of sex, race, religion or belief, ethnic or national origin, disability, age, citizenship, marital, domestic or civil partnership status, sexual orientation, gender identity, veteran status, pregnancy or related condition (including breastfeeding) or any other basis as protected by applicable law. For more information visit Careers at Wayve. To learn more about what drives us, visit Values at Wayve DISCLAIMER: We will not ask about marriage or pregnancy, care responsibilities or disabilities in any of our job adverts or interviews. However, we do look to capture information about care responsibilities, and disabilities among other diversity information as part of an optional DEI Monitoring form to help us identify areas of improvement in our hiring process and ensure that the process is inclusive and non-discriminatory. title: Senior Manager - Capital Allowances

Working closely with our capital allowances lead, you'll advise senior finance teams, oversee technical quality and commercial performance, develop colleagues and win new work. Advise on plant and machinery allowances, structures and buildings allowances, land remediation relief and the tax treatment of fixed assets. Support property acquisitions, disposals and wider transactions, including due diligence, expenditure apportionments and capital allowances elections. Analyse fixed asset registers, construction cost information and supporting documentation, working with clients, surveyors and other advisers to identify qualifying expenditure. Strong technical knowledge of UK capital allowances legislation, with experience advising on property transactions and major capital expenditure projects. CTA, ACA, ACCA, RICS or an equivalent relevant qualification. Experience interpreting financial data, construction costs and technical documentation to support robust claims. Commercial judgement, including managing engagement profitability and contributing to winning new work. Experience managing and developing colleagues, with confidence reviewing work and resolving technical issues. Clear communication skills and credibility with CFOs, finance directors and other senior stakeholders. Confidence using digital tools and a practical interest in applying AI and automation to advisory work. An adaptable, collaborative approach and an appetite to help build a growing practice. You'll join the global Salesforce team for 12 months to make the CRM faster, clearer and more intuitive. This is a hands-on build role. You'll design the experience and code it in Lightning Web Components, working with Sales, RevOps, Marketing and Data, and directly with the reps who use the result. What You Will Do Redesign the rep experience Audit the current Lightning experience (record pages, console apps, list views, home pages) and find where reps lose time to clicks, clutter and missing context. Turn what you find into a prioritised roadmap of UI improvements tied to rep productivity and adoption. Design and prototype improved layouts, workflows and components, and validate them with reps before building. Build with LWC Develop custom Lightning Web Components (and supporting Apex where needed) that replace clunky standard layouts with focused, usable interfaces. Configure and extend Lightning App Builder pages, Dynamic Forms, Dynamic Actions and console apps to deliver a consistent experience across teams and regions. Build reusable components and follow SLDS conventions so the UI stays consistent and maintainable after your contract ends. Make it stick Run feedback sessions, usability tests and pilots with reps and managers, and iterate on the results. Track adoption, page performance and user satisfaction to show what each release changed. Create release notes, short walkthroughs and handover documentation so changes land well and the team can maintain what you build. Work as part of the global team Work within the global team's standards for source control, code review, sandboxes and release management. Partner with admins, architects and data teams so UI changes fit the wider data model, security model and automation. Pass on what you learn about Lightning UX patterns and LWC best practices to the wider team. What You Will Need Must have Strong, demonstrable experience building Lightning Web Components in production. Solid Apex, SOQL and Salesforce data model knowledge to support your components. Deep knowledge of Lightning Experience customisation: App Builder, Dynamic Forms, page layouts, console apps and Flows. Experience with Salesforce DX, Git and a CI/CD or deployment process. A UX mindset: you start from user problems, can explain design decisions, and can take feedback from non-technical users. Clear communication and the ability to work independently across time zones in a global team. Nice to have Portfolio or examples of Salesforce UI work you've shipped (screenshots or demos are ideal). Experience with SLDS, Figma or similar prototyping tools, and accessibility (WCAG) principles. Experience in Sales Cloud, especially rep-facing workflows such as opportunity management, account planning and pipeline views. Jest testing for LWC, and Salesforce certifications (Platform Developer I/II, JavaScript Developer I, Platform App Builder). Experience with performance profiling and optimisation in Lightning pages. Month 6: First wave of redesigned pages and components live for a pilot group, with adoption and feedback baselined. Month 12: Redesigned experience rolled out to target teams, a maintained component library in place, and full documentation handed to the global team. Built to tackle the time-consuming, manual work that gets in the way of real work, our tools automate everything from travel bookings to expenses, invoice processing, and more. By eliminating this shadow work that wastes hours, erodes morale, and saps innovation, we're on a mission to power real work, with real impact. We're trusted by more than 12,000 companies worldwide, including Bolt, GoCardless, and Fabletics, and we're tackling the 7 hours of lost productivity per employee each week, a $1.7 trillion problem . Founded in 2015, Perk has grown into a global company of more than 1,800 people across 12 offices globally, with headquarters in London and Boston. title: Claims and Returns Coordinator
description: Zip Water is an industry leading filtered boiling, chilled and sparkling water specialist, known globally for being home to the world’s most advanced range of drinking water solutions. We provide businesses and homes in more than 70 countries with an extensive range of high-quality drinking and hot water solutions, designed to transform the way individuals, organisations and businesses provide water, for good. We are pleased to announce this exciting opportunity to join our Supply Chain team as a Claims & Returns Coordinator. This role is responsible for the end-to-end management, administration and continuous improvement of customer returns, carrier collections and transport claims processes. The role acts as the central coordination point between Customer Service, Logistics, Warehouse, Finance, Sales and external carriers to ensure returned goods, collection activities, customer credits and claims recoveries are managed efficiently and professionally. The position will also drive return reduction initiatives, identify root causes, improve customer experience, maximize recovery of costs from carriers and customers, and provide KPI reporting and governance across the returns and claim function. This is an office-based role to be close to the warehouse returns and logistic teams. Core Role & Responsibilities: • Manage the complete Return Authorization (RAN) process from request through to closure. • Coordinate customer returns and carrier collections. • Manage transport damage, shortage, loss and non-delivery claims. • Gather evidence and submit claims within carrier deadlines. • Track claim progress and maximize recoveries. • Maintain ERP/WMS return records. • Produce KPI reports and trend analysis. • Conduct root cause analysis and implement corrective actions. • Support customer credits and recharge processes. • Drive continuous improvement initiatives. Experience in processing claims with logistics companies such as DPD, DHL, etc, is essential Requirements Experience in logistics, returns, claims or customer service administration. Strong Excel, ERP/WMS, communication, analytical and problem-solving skills. Great attention to detail & organisation skills Customer focused to ensure great service is delivered Commercially aware Ability to take a proactive approach to assigned workload Benefits 25 days annual leave + bank holidays Flexible working available Company Sick Pay (after qualifying period) Full training and continuous support with your team Modern canteen and break “chill out” areas There’s onsite parking – we have plenty of space!!
